methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $33M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Molten Industries, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Caleb Boyd and Kevin Bush, has raised $32.9M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company in the robotics and manufacturing sector, with peer valuations ranging from seed stage (Walden Robotics, $1.1B) through Series B (Generalist AI $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics $1.8B, Dexterity $1.6B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression methodology, using total raised as a proxy baseline, applied a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $66M. Peer-median analysis across the four same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables produced a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The disparity between methods reflects the heterogeneity within the peer set—particularly the inclusion of later-stage Series B companies alongside an earlier-stage seed reference.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $56M (conservative stage-progression floor) to $2.0B (peer median ceiling), with a midpoint of $883M. The wide band reflects uncertainty around stage-appropriate comparability: the peer set skews meaningfully later than Molten's Series A position. A defensible valuation likely clusters in the $150M–$400M range pending clarity on capital efficiency, technical differentiation, and near-term funding milestones relative to the peer cohort.
